figure: Figure 9.1 — Ring traffic and directional bandwidth
issue: The annotation says “140 GB tensor” while the x-axis and surrounding prose define the quantity as logical input tensor per rank. A reader can misread the annotation as a 140 GB total tensor rather than 140 GB per rank.
evidence: The x-axis label is “Logical input tensor per rank (GB)”; the annotation reads “140 GB tensor (245 GB sent at 1.75×)”; the caption says “At 140 GB the ideal times are about 0.54 s, 6.1 s and 98 s.” The prose on printed p. 162 says the eight-rank ring “sends 245 GB per rank.”
acceptance_test: Change the annotation to “140 GB per rank” or “140 GB logical tensor per rank,” and verify the caption uses the same per-rank qualifier at least once.

issue: The parenthetical “(8 B/rank)” is ambiguous: it can be read as the amount each rank sends, but the figure later states each rank sends 12 B across both phases. The 8 B is the input size per rank, not the communication volume.
evidence: The figure header says “Four ranks; four FP16 elements per input (8 B/rank).” The reduce-scatter and all-gather annotations each say “6 B sent + 6 B received/rank,” and the bottom box says “Per rank: 12 B sent + 12 B received = 24 B endpoint total.”
acceptance_test: Replace “(8 B/rank)” with “(8 B input per rank)” or “(8 B payload per rank before communication),” and confirm the caption still states the 12 B sent / 12 B received total.

figure: Figure 9.3 — The payload path is not the bootstrap path
issue: The dashed red setup arrows are thin and low-contrast relative to the solid black payload arrows. In grayscale they become mid-gray dashed lines, and at print size the connection from the setup box to ProcessGroupNCCL/ProcessGroupXCCL is easy to miss.
evidence: The legend distinguishes “Payload / execution” as a solid black arrow and “Control / setup” as a dashed red arrow. The dashed red lines run from the top setup box down the outside of the framework-backend boxes; they are visibly lighter and thinner than the solid arrows.
acceptance_test: Increase the dashed setup-line weight or contrast, or add a short direct label on each dashed connector (“setup only”), and inspect a grayscale print proof to confirm the dashed path remains immediately visible.

figure: Figure 10.1 — Three parallelism patterns, one per panel
issue: Panel A labels the all-reduce communication step in a floating red dashed box below the GPUs, but no arrows connect the GPUs to that box or the box to “full output.” The communication step is therefore visually detached from the computation it summarizes.
evidence: Panel A shows GPU 0 and GPU 1 with weight shards W0 and W1, then a red dashed box reading “all-reduce partial sums → full output” beneath them. There are no connector arrows from the GPU boxes into or out of the all-reduce box.
acceptance_test: Add arrows from GPU 0 and GPU 1 into the all-reduce box and from the all-reduce box to a “full output” label, or redraw the all-reduce as a connected stage in the panel-A flow.

figure: Figure 10.1 — Three parallelism patterns, one per panel
issue: Panel B says “idle (bubble) at fill/drain — pipeline-wide” but the diagram does not visually encode the bubble. The panel shows only three sequential stage boxes and arrows; the key pipeline-parallel cost is asserted in text rather than shown.
evidence: Panel B draws GPU 0 (layers 1–8), GPU 1 (layers 9–16), and GPU 2 (layers 17–24) with P2P arrows. The only representation of the fill/drain bubble is the text line “idle (bubble) at fill/drain — pipeline-wide.”
acceptance_test: Add a small schedule strip or shaded idle intervals at the start and end of the pipeline, or explicitly state in the caption that the bubble is not drawn and is only named; then verify the panel still reads correctly in grayscale.
